messages:
mira: heads up — us-central1-gpu pool showing a spike in local disk tail latency on small-block writes, scheduler is holding GPU pods in Pending
alex: saw the dashboard spike. How many nodes are affected?
infra-bot: Alert: storage-iops-anomaly detected on us-central1; affected_nodes=12; avg_write_latency p99: 200ms -> 2.4s; triggered=2026-03-21T12:07:43Z
mira: quick snip from affected node (iostat 1s sample):
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 10.00 120.00 512.00 4096.00 32.0 8.2 65.3 1.2 95.5
```
— lots of small write bursts, avgqu-sz jumping before pods stall
jordan: scheduler logs show repeated backoff: "node disk pressure" and kubelet marking ephemeral-storage pressure briefly. Could be janitor overlap or a compaction job
mira: confirmed — background overlayfs GC and our janitor were both running. janitor.concurrency currently = 8 on the AMI image
alex: last time we saw this, dropping janitor concurrency helped. can we set to 2 and roll?
mira: rolling a config change now to set janitor.concurrency=2 and lowering its io_priority. also going to bump cleaner process ionice to idle
sam: FYI — customer-facing GPU jobs are queuing. what's expected capacity hit?
alex: ballpark ~18% fewer GPUs usable in that pool while the nodes are busy; if we evacuate and run in other regions it'll add ~$10k/day in cross-region burst costs
jordan: temporary mitigation option: cordon the 12 nodes and drain non-critical pods to healthier nodes in us-east1. affinity-sensitive pods will need manual fixes
mira: starting cordon/drain for 6 less-critical nodes now: `kubectl cordon gnode-082 && kubectl drain gnode-082 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
mira: update 12:20 UTC — drain hit 4 pods that couldn't reschedule due to strict nodeAffinity. patched the Deployment with soft-affinity and re-triggered evictions
alex: also kicking off a canary kernel tweak to increase NVMe IO queue depth on the AMI from 128 -> 256 (2 nodes first) to see if queueing behavior improves
infra-bot: Deploy job queued: nvme-qdepth-bump (canary) on gnode-ctl-023, gnode-ctl-045
sam: quick note from cost ops — if we start bursting into spare capacity, tag me. prefer throttling scheduler or selective evictions over full cross-region fallback
jordan: long term ideas: add a Prom alert for small-block tail p99 > 800ms, and a probe for janitor.concurrency spikes so we catch overlapping maintenance jobs
mira: agreed. also adding a temporary guard in scheduler: if node.io_wait_ms > 500 then avoid scheduling new GPU jobs for 60s to reduce thrash
alex: post-mitigation numbers: after cordons, p99 dropped to ~120ms on the remaining nodes. monitoring for 30m before uncordoning
sam: thanks all — please @me on the postmortem draft. we'll need cost impact + runbook steps
alex: noted. I'll open a short postmortem and attach graphs.
mira: will follow up with exact janitor config diff and kernel patch links. :thumbsup:
